scope_question: As of 2026-07-07, HearthSim deckstrings remains the correct deterministic basis for pre-run deck intake because the official format and current Python reference implementation decode the deckstring into hero DBF IDs, format, canonical card DBF/count pairs, and sideboards without strategy inference. HearthstoneJSON `cards.json` remains the correct normalized registry layer for DBF-to-CardID joins and broad static semantics because it publishes unique `id`, `dbfId`, localized `text`, `type`, `mechanics`, and non-collectible rows such as heroes and hero powers. However, a live 2026-07-07 probe of `https://api.hearthstonejson.com/v1/latest/enUS/cards.json` showed `heroPowerDbfId` on 2,988 rows and `questReward` on 9 rows, but `entourage` on 0 rows and `playRequirements` on 0 rows; Shadowform (`EX1_625`) and Darkbishop Benedictus (`SW_448`) also expose the hero-power change only through card text or tags, not through a direct structured replacement link, so HearthstoneJSON alone is not a full generated-entity or hero-power-transform authority.
confirmed_facts: For a lean pre-run config skill, the right foundation is: 1. decode the submitted deck code with HearthSim deckstrings or an equivalent implementation that preserves exact DBF identity, hero identity, counts, format, and sideboards; 2. join those DBF IDs to exact CardIDs and static card metadata through HearthstoneJSON `cards.json` or an equivalent full card registry; 3. treat static card text, mechanics, and tags as source-backed semantic inputs for pre-run planning; 4. add a deterministic supplement layer for non-deck entities that current live HearthstoneJSON does not link cleanly, especially transformed hero powers, quest rewards, option cards, and generated entities; 5. fail closed for runtime-writing decisions when exact CardID lineage cannot be proven. Hero-power transform semantics are a valid pre-run concept when the source card effect is explicit and deterministic, but they should not rely on free-form text parsing alone when the runtime package needs an exact replacement CardID.
implementation_implications: The current HSConfig repository aligns with most of that design. `README.md` already defines HSConfig as a direct pre-game config authoring tool. `src/hsconfig/deckstring_decode.py` uses `hearthstone.deckstrings.parse_deckstring`, preserves hero DBF identity, format, main-deck cards, and sideboards, and emits a deckstring decode receipt. `src/hsconfig/hearthstonejson.py` already normalizes the live HearthstoneJSON payload into exact `id`, `dbf_id`, `text`, `mechanics`, `referenced_tags`, `hero_power_dbf_id`, `quest_reward`, `play_requirements`, and `entourage` fields. `src/hsconfig/semantic_enrichment.py` already recognizes the Shadowform and Benedictus gap and supplements it with a deterministic `Mind Spike` fallback plus deckwide `replace_starting_hero_power` effects when required. `src/hsconfig/card_behavior_surface_router.py` and `tests/test_card_behavior_router.py` already model `hero_power_transform` as a first-class runtime-lowering concept, and `tests/test_config_readiness.py` proves that a source-backed `hero_power_transform` claim can be satisfied by the GlobalValues lane when no meaningful per-card CardID row is required. A targeted local verification run on 2026-07-07 passed: `test_card_metadata.py`, `test_hero_power_transform_claim_routes_to_hero_power_surface`, and `test_source_backed_hero_power_transform_can_be_satisfied_by_globalvalues`.

risks_or_gaps: Current `src/hsconfig/deckstring_decode.py` resolves DBF IDs through `hearthstone.cardxml.load_dbf()` rather than through HearthstoneJSON, so the repo still uses two metadata authorities for different parts of the pipeline. That is workable, but it makes source-precedence and build-freshness rules more important.
HearthSim deckstrings is only a decode authority. It does not provide card text, non-deck entity links, or exact runtime semantics by itself.

Live HearthstoneJSON currently exposes zero populated `entourage` rows and zero populated `playRequirements` rows in `cards.json`, so HSConfig cannot assume that documented field families are currently sufficient for generated pools, option branches, or targeting closure.

Shadowform-style and Benedictus-style hero-power replacement is not safely derivable from deck decode alone. The source card text proves the semantic change, but the exact replacement hero power CardID still needs a curated or registry-backed supplement when the live structured payload does not name it directly.
Text- or tag-only semantic lowering is appropriate for report generation and some GlobalValues posture overlays, but it is not by itself a safe basis for every per-card runtime write.

If HSConfig ever treats generated-entity inference from plain text as authoritative without an exact identity supplement, it can silently emit wrong CardID ownership for option cards, transformed powers, or created cards.
recommendation: Keep the current architectural split, but formalize the authority order. Use HearthSim deckstrings as the immutable deck decode layer, use HearthstoneJSON `cards.json` as the primary normalized CardID and static-semantics registry, and keep a small deterministic supplement layer for exact non-deck identities that the live payload does not expose cleanly. Then make the pre-run skill fail closed whenever a required transformed hero power, generated card, or option-card CardID cannot be proven from structured data plus that curated supplement.
